bench.heading: Against another forecaster
bench.intro: Beating a base rate is a low bar. chancedegol.com.br publishes, for every played match, the probabilities it gave beforehand — so both models can be scored on identical matches. Their probabilities sum to 1.000, so this is model against model, with no bookmaker margin to strip out.
bench.rps_callout: RPS — Ranked Probability Score. The standard metric for 1X2 forecasts. Home, draw and away are ordered: a draw sits between a home win and an away win. RPS works on cumulative probabilities, so predicting a home win costs less when the match is drawn than when the away side wins. Brier treats the three as unrelated labels and charges the same either way. Lower is better; 0 is perfect.
calibration.chart_title: Forecast relegation probability vs. what happened
calibration.heading: Is the model calibrated?
calibration.intro:
A forecast of 40% should come true about 40% of the time. This pools every relegation
  forecast across all eleven seasons and asks whether it does.
calibration.trap_callout_p1: The trap that made us retract an earlier finding. A club sitting in the same probability band for two months contributes sixty forecasts and exactly one outcome. Counting forecasts as the sample size makes a handful of clubs look like a large, decisive dataset — and it made a "relegation overconfidence" result look real when it was noise.
calibration.trap_callout_p2: So the observed rate below is computed per club, one club one outcome, and each point carries a 95% interval reflecting how few clubs that really is.
coverage.heading: What the archive is made of
coverage.intro2: A date simulated 10 times cannot express a probability finer than 10%: every number it produces is a multiple of one tenth. The thin dates column counts how many fell under 1,000 iterations — 2025 had 79 such dates before it was rebuilt.
heat.heading: Where does each club finish?
heat.intro:
Title and relegation are two slices of something richer: on every date the simulator
  produces a full distribution over all twenty places. This is that distribution — one row
  per club, one column per finishing place, darker meaning more likely. Drag the slider to move
  through the season and watch certainty build.
heat.key_complete: Outlined cell = where the club actually finished
heat.key_incomplete: Season still being played — no final places yet

points.heading: How many points keep you up?
points.intro1: This has no league-wide answer, and averaging one out would be misleading. The cut fell on 36 points in 2019 and on 43 in 2017 — whether a total is safe depends entirely on how tightly bunched the bottom of that table is. And a finished season has no probabilities left in it: a club on 44 points either went down or it did not.
points.intro2:
So this is one season, from one date, conditioned on the standings at that
  moment and the fixtures still to play. Move the date slider back to watch a live
  season's answer sharpen as the season closes.

model.elo.name: Elo
model.elo.lede: Every simulation this model has produced, replayed day by day across eleven seasons. Each club carries one Elo rating, updated after every match it plays in Série A, Série B, the Copa do Brasil and the Libertadores or Sudamericana. On each as-of date the gap between two clubs' ratings sets the expected goal difference, each club's recent matches set how many goals to expect, and the simulator plays out the rest of the season to a full table — giving a title probability, a relegation probability and a complete finishing-position distribution for all twenty clubs on every matchday.
model.elo.bench: That erases the edge chancedegol holds over the incumbent, but the interval still touches zero: read it as parity or slightly better, not a clear lead.
model.elo.coverage: The Elo archive runs 20,000 simulations on every date, the same depth as the incumbent’s. It was built in three passes — 1,000, then 2,000, then 20,000 per date — each adding to the same results, so the counts below are totals.
model.elo.method: Probabilities come from the elo simulator at its default settings: K 20, home advantage 85, division seeds 1500 / 1400 / 1300 / 1450, a 1 / 1.75 / 2.5 goal-margin ladder, and a goal-difference line refitted each season on the season before. A 24-setting sweep across ten seasons found none better.
model.incumbent.name: the incumbent
model.incumbent.lede:
Every simulation this model has produced, replayed day by day across eleven
  seasons. Each as-of date re-estimates every club's scoring rates from its last 19 matches at
  that venue, then simulates the rest of the season to a full table — giving a title
  probability, a relegation probability and a complete finishing-position distribution for all
  twenty clubs on every matchday.
model.incumbent.bench: chancedegol is ahead in most seasons. The gap is small and its interval just touches zero, but it is consistent — and Elo, fed every competition a club plays, closes it.
model.incumbent.coverage: Iteration counts are not uniform, and not even uniform within a season. Nine seasons ran a fixed 20,000 per date. 2024 and 2025 were built up incrementally during those seasons at whatever budget was passed at the time, so their counts vary date to date.
model.incumbent.method: Probabilities come from the batch simulator at the model's default constants: a 19-match per-venue lookback, 4/3/1 recency weights, a 50/50 home-attack / away-defence blend, and the newcomer prior at full strength. All four were swept across ten seasons and none was beaten by more than noise.

v2.table.heading: Every club, every outcome
v2.table.intro: Pick a season and slide to any forecast date. Clubs are ordered by the place they finish on average across the simulated seasons, and every chance is marked by how likely it is — in the colour of what a club is chasing, and in red for the drop.
v2.table.note: From {iterations} simulated seasons on this date. Top 4 and top 6 are the places that usually carry Libertadores spots; the exact number moves each year with the cup winners. The place column is the latest table, or the final one, not the table on the chosen date.
race.floor_note: Below 0.5% the figure is not trustworthy: 20,000 simulated seasons cannot tell 1 in 20,000 from zero, so clubs in that range are shown together, without a percentage.
